programs.name: California Federal Surplus Property Program

programs.fullDescription: The California Department of General Services' Federal Surplus Personal Property Program (FSPP) obtains federal surplus property for qualifying public agencies and nonprofit organizations ("donees") in California, for a service and handling fee instead of the full cost.
programs.whatTheyOffer:
- Federal surplus personal property for your organization's operations
- Items may include furniture, office equipment, vehicles, electronics, tools, and more (availability varies)
- Service and handling fee instead of purchase price (flat $100 or a percentage of original acquisition cost, e.g. 0-30% for items under $15,000)
programs.howToGetIt:
1. Check the federal eligibility guidelines (public agencies, schools, libraries, museums, nonprofit health providers, providers serving homeless or low-income people, programs for older adults, certain veterans and service organizations, and volunteer fire departments)
2. Submit the donee eligibility application to DGS
3. Once approved, request available federal surplus property
4. Agree to use restrictions and pay the service and handling fee
5. Pick up items directly or arrange your own pickup

programs.name: CalVet Benefits & Services Portal
programs.description: Free benefits information and navigation for California veterans and families; access to CalVet home loans, college fee waivers, veterans homes, and employment services
programs.fullDescription: The California Department of Veterans Affairs (CalVet) connects California veterans and their families with their earned state and federal benefits through education, advocacy, and direct services. The CalVet website helps veterans find housing, education, employment, healthcare, and financial assistance.
programs.whatTheyOffer:
- myCalVet profile for customized benefits and services information
- Home loans with competitive rates (CalVet Home Loans)
- College fee waivers for dependents (CalVet College Fee Waiver)
- Veterans Homes of California (8 locations statewide)
- Employment and transition services
- Help with VA claims through County Veterans Service Offices (CVSOs)
- Mental health and wellness resources
- Veteran designation on driver licenses and ID cards
programs.howToGetIt:
1. Visit calvet.ca.gov or call CalVet toll-free
2. Create a myCalVet profile to get customized benefits information
3. Find your local County Veterans Service Office (CVSO) at 1-844-737-8838 (1-844-SERV-VET) for free in-person help with claims and applications
4. Apply for the specific programs you qualify for
programs.keywords: CalVet, veteran benefits, California veteran, VA benefits, home loan, college fee waiver, veterans home, employment, claims assistance

programs.name: Disabled Veteran Business Enterprise (DVBE) Program
programs.description: DVBE certification helps disabled veteran-owned businesses access California state contracts under a 3% statewide participation goal
programs.fullDescription: California's Disabled Veteran Business Enterprise (DVBE) certification, administered by the Department of General Services' Office of Small Business and DVBE Services (OSDS), helps businesses owned and run by disabled veterans compete for state contracts. The state's goal is to award at least 3% of its overall annual contract dollars to certified DVBEs.
programs.whatTheyOffer:
- DVBE certification recognized by California state agencies
- Eligibility for the DVBE Participation Program (3% statewide contract goal)
- "SB/DVBE Option": state agencies can contract directly with certified DVBEs (with quotes from at least two) for goods, services, IT, and public works above $5,000, up to set limits
- Free certification workshops and outreach events
programs.howToGetIt:
1. The veteran must have a service-connected disability of at least 10% and live in California
2. The business must be at least 51% owned by one or more disabled veterans (LLCs must be wholly owned) and managed day-to-day by disabled veterans
3. The home office must be located in the U.S.
4. Register your business on Cal eProcure and complete the online certification application
5. Submit requested documents, including federal tax returns for the past three years
programs.keywords: DVBE, disabled veteran, business certification, state contracts, government contracts, veteran-owned, procurement, bid preference

programs.name: California Transition Assistance Program (CalTAP)
programs.description: Free transition assistance connecting veterans to benefits, education, employment, and entrepreneurship resources
programs.fullDescription: CalVet's California Transition Assistance Program (CalTAP) informs and connects veterans of all eras to their earned federal and state benefits, and provides continued support as their needs change, through five pathways - Core Curriculum, Education, Employment, Entrepreneurship, and Service Providers.
programs.whatTheyOffer:
- Core curriculum: Veteran 101, California benefits, and financial literacy
- Education pathway: choosing a school and using education benefits
- Employment pathway: apprenticeships, job search, and state employment
- Entrepreneurship pathway: DVBE certification and business resources
- Connections to service providers (attorneys, employers, primary care, supportive housing)
- Free virtual and in-person workshops and recorded webinars
programs.howToGetIt:
1. Visit the CalTAP page to find upcoming workshops or watch past webinars
2. Submit a CalTAP Request for Response to ask about benefits, County Veterans Service Offices, or pathways
3. Or email CalTAP@calvet.ca.gov
4. Community partners can request CalTAP workshops, presentations, or resource tables
programs.keywords: CalTAP, veteran transition, military transition, separating service member, education, employment, entrepreneurship, benefits navigation

programs.fullDescription: Santa Clara County's 24/7 Crisis and Suicide Prevention Lifeline (988) provides immediate support for mental health and substance use crises and connects callers to county behavioral health services and mobile response teams.

- Referrals to county behavioral health services

programs.howToGetIt: Call or text 988 anytime. If your phone doesn't have a 408, 650, or 669 area code, call 1-800-704-0900 and press 1 to reach Santa Clara County's local counselors. The same 800 number is for non-emergency behavioral health questions. Free, anonymous, and confidential.

programs.howToGetIt: Call or text 988 anytime. Calls from Marin are answered by Buckelew's local 988 counselors. Marin County's resource guide also lists Buckelew's local hotline at 415-499-1100.
programs.keywords: Marin County, suicide prevention, Buckelew Programs, 988, crisis hotline, grief support group, Allies for Hope

programs.name: Napa County Mental Health Crisis Line

programs.fullDescription: Napa County's 24-hour mental health crisis hotline provides immediate support for Napa County residents of all ages experiencing a mental health crisis or emergency.
programs.whatTheyOffer:
- 24/7 crisis support for all ages

- Crisis Stabilization Services (short-term care lasting less than 24 hours)

programs.howToGetIt: Call 707-253-4711, 24 hours a day. The Crisis Stabilization Services Program is at 2751 Napa Valley Corporate Way, Building B, Napa. For a life-threatening emergency, call 911.

programs.name: Solano County Crisis Line

programs.whatTheyOffer:

programs.howToGetIt: Call Mobile Crisis at 707-806-0866 anytime for an urgent mental health crisis, such as suicidal thoughts. For non-urgent mental health and substance use services, call the Behavioral Health Access Line at 800-547-0495. You can also call or text 988.
programs.keywords: Solano County, crisis line, mobile crisis, mental health crisis, suicide prevention, Crisis Stabilization Unit

programs.howToGetIt: Call 888-670-1360 anytime (toll-free in California). No appointment or application. For regular outbound check-in calls, fill out the intake form online. Other languages - Spanish 888-571-0411, Cantonese/Mandarin 888-670-2504, Tagalog 888-570-0867, Vietnamese 888-670-1361, Korean 888-560-7684, Russian 888-560-7360.
programs.keywords: Friendship Line, Institute on Aging, senior crisis, loneliness, isolation, companionship, grief support, caregivers, 60+

programs.name: Denti-Cal
programs.description: Medi-Cal Dental (formerly called Denti-Cal) is California's Medicaid dental program, providing free or low-cost dental care to Medi-Cal members of all ages.
programs.fullDescription: Medi-Cal Dental (formerly called Denti-Cal) is California's Medicaid dental program, providing free or low-cost dental care to Medi-Cal members of all ages.
programs.whatTheyOffer:
- Preventive care (cleanings, exams, x-rays, fluoride)
- Restorative services (fillings, crowns)
- Extractions and oral surgery
- Dentures and partials
- Emergency dental services
- Orthodontics for children under 21 (when medically necessary)
programs.howToGetIt: If you have Medi-Cal, dental benefits are included. Find a Medi-Cal dentist with the online Find-A-Dentist search or call the Medi-Cal Dental Telephone Service Center at 1-800-322-6384 (free call, Mon-Fri 8am-5pm). Starting July 1, 2027, some adult members will lose full dental benefits based on immigration status (emergency dental care stays covered); children under 19, pregnant and postpartum members, and former foster youth under 26 keep full benefits.
programs.keywords: Denti-Cal, Medi-Cal Dental, Medicaid dental, free dental, Medi-Cal, cleanings, fillings, extractions, dentures, orthodontics, oral surgery

programs.name: EyeCare America
programs.description: EyeCare America is a public service program of the American Academy of Ophthalmology that matches uninsured and underinsured adults 18+ with volunteer ophthalmologists for a medical eye exam at no out-of-pocket cost.
programs.fullDescription: EyeCare America is a public service program of the American Academy of Ophthalmology that matches uninsured and underinsured adults 18+ with volunteer ophthalmologists for a medical eye exam at no out-of-pocket cost.
programs.whatTheyOffer:
- Medical eye exam by a volunteer ophthalmologist
- Up to one year of follow-up visits for conditions found at the first exam
- No out-of-pocket cost for covered exam and follow-up care
- Does NOT cover glasses, contacts, eyeglass prescriptions, surgery, medications, or tests
- One-time referral program
programs.howToGetIt: You must be 18 or older, a US citizen or legal resident, have no HMO, PPO, private insurance, or VA benefits, not have seen an ophthalmologist in 3+ years, and not have used EyeCare America before. Fill out the online referral questionnaire to get matched right away, or call 877-887-6327 (Mon-Fri 8am-2pm PT). Not for urgent eye problems.
programs.keywords: EyeCare America, free eye exam, medical eye exam, uninsured, underinsured, glaucoma, ophthalmologist, American Academy of Ophthalmology

programs.name: Medi-Cal (Medicaid)
programs.description: Medi-Cal is California's Medicaid program, providing free or low-cost health coverage to millions of Californians including low-income adults, families, seniors, pregnant women, and people with disabilities.
programs.fullDescription: Medi-Cal is California's Medicaid program, providing free or low-cost health coverage to millions of Californians including low-income adults, families, seniors, pregnant women, and people with disabilities.
programs.whatTheyOffer:
- Doctor and hospital visits
- Prescription medications
- Preventive care and screenings
- Mental health services
- Dental care (Medi-Cal Dental)
- Vision care
- Substance use treatment
- Long-term care services
programs.howToGetIt: Apply online at CoveredCA.com or BenefitsCal.com, through your county social services office, or by phone with Covered California at 1-800-300-1506 (Mon-Fri 8am-6pm). Adults generally qualify with income up to 138% of the poverty level (266% for children), or if they get CalFresh, SSI/SSP, or CalWORKs. You can apply any time of year and must renew once a year. Some benefits for certain adults are changing based on immigration status, so check with your county office.
programs.keywords: Medi-Cal, Medicaid, free health insurance, low-income, doctor, hospital, prescription, mental health, dental, vision, CoveredCA

programs.whatTheyOffer:

- Treatment referrals in your area
- Information about mental health and substance use
- Support in English and Spanish
- Referrals to local support groups
- Information about state-funded treatment programs
- Help finding sliding-scale or free treatment
programs.howToGetIt: Call 1-800-662-4357 anytime, 24/7, 365 days a year. Specialists will connect you with local treatment facilities, support groups, and community organizations. TTY available at 1-800-487-4889. You can also text your ZIP code to 435748 (HELP4U) or search FindTreatment.gov. The helpline does not provide counseling.

programs.howToGetIt: Apply online at VA.gov, by phone at 1-877-222-8387, or in person at any VA medical center. You'll need your DD214 or other discharge documents. Most veterans who served on active duty are eligible.

programs.name: WIC (Women, Infants, Children)
programs.description: WIC is a nutrition program providing healthy food, nutrition education, breastfeeding support, and healthcare referrals to pregnant and postpartum women, infants, and children under 5 in California.
programs.fullDescription: WIC is a nutrition program providing healthy food, nutrition education, breastfeeding support, and healthcare referrals to pregnant and postpartum women, infants, and children under 5 in California.
programs.whatTheyOffer:
- Monthly benefits for nutritious foods (fruits, vegetables, whole grains, milk, eggs)
- Infant formula and baby food
- Nutrition education and counseling
- Breastfeeding support and breast pumps
- Health screenings and referrals
- Farmers' market benefits
- WIC card accepted at most grocery stores
programs.howToGetIt: Contact your local WIC office, call 1-888-942-9675 (24 hours), or call 1-800-852-5770 during business hours. You'll need proof of income (up to 185% of poverty level; families on Medi-Cal or CalFresh usually qualify automatically), residency, and identity. Pregnant women, new mothers, infants, and children under 5 may qualify, and dads, grandparents, and foster parents of young children can apply too.

programs.fullDescription: San Mateo County Behavioral Health and Recovery Services provides mental health and substance use treatment, prevention, and recovery services to residents of all ages in San Mateo County.

programs.howToGetIt: Call the Access Call Center at 1-800-686-0101 (TDD 1-800-943-2833) for consultation, assessment, and referral. programs.name: CalRx OTC Naloxone Nasal Spray
programs.description: CalRx is California's initiative to make naloxone, a life-saving medication that reverses opioid overdoses, affordable and accessible to all residents without a prescription.
programs.fullDescription: CalRx is California's initiative to make naloxone, a life-saving medication that reverses opioid overdoses, affordable and accessible to all residents without a prescription.
programs.whatTheyOffer:
- 4mg naloxone nasal spray (Narcan-equivalent)
- Twin pack for $19 plus shipping and handling
- No prescription required
- Well below typical retail price
- Simple nasal spray administration
- Organizations may qualify for free naloxone through the state Naloxone Distribution Project
programs.howToGetIt: Anyone living in California can order online at calrxnaloxone.com (linked from the CalRx page). Orders must ship to a California address, and the minimum order is one twin pack. Naloxone cannot be resold.
programs.keywords: CalRx, naloxone, Narcan, opioid overdose, fentanyl, overdose reversal, nasal spray, opioid crisis, harm reduction, OTC

programs.name: Naloxone Distribution Project (NDP)
programs.description: California's Naloxone Distribution Project provides free naloxone and fentanyl test strips to eligible organizations working to prevent opioid overdose deaths in their communities. It does not serve individuals directly.
programs.fullDescription: California's Naloxone Distribution Project provides free naloxone and fentanyl test strips to eligible organizations working to prevent opioid overdose deaths in their communities. It does not serve individuals directly.
programs.whatTheyOffer:
- Free naloxone nasal spray (generic or Narcan brand)
- Free fentanyl test strips
- Shipped directly to approved organizations
- Available to eligible organizations statewide
programs.howToGetIt: Organizations apply through the Department of Health Care Services' online NDP application. Eligible entities include community organizations (harm reduction groups, opioid coalitions), schools and universities, tribal entities, county public health and behavioral health departments, fire/EMS and first responders, and law enforcement. Fentanyl test strip requests require a business license, FEIN, or tax-exempt letter. Individuals can buy low-cost naloxone through CalRx.
programs.keywords: NDP, naloxone, Narcan, free, nonprofit, fentanyl test strips, harm reduction, overdose prevention, opioid, community distribution

programs.name: AIDS Drug Assistance Program (ADAP)

programs.fullDescription: California's AIDS Drug Assistance Program provides life-saving HIV/AIDS medications and health insurance assistance to low-income Californians living with HIV who lack adequate coverage.
programs.whatTheyOffer:
- Free FDA-approved HIV/AIDS medications on the ADAP formulary
- Premium payment assistance for private health insurance (OA-HIPP)
- Premium payment assistance for Medicare Part C and Part D plans
- For California residents 18+ with income up to 600% FPL (MAGI)
- For people not fully covered by Medi-Cal or other insurance
programs.howToGetIt: Make an appointment with a certified ADAP Enrollment Worker at an ADAP enrollment site (use the state's site locator or call the ADAP call center at 844-421-7050, Monday-Friday 8am-5pm). programs.keywords: ADAP, AIDS, HIV, antiretroviral, medication, free, insurance assistance, OA-HIPP, Medicare, undocumented, HIV drugs

programs.fullDescription: The California Home Visiting Program provides free, voluntary home visits to pregnant and newly parenting families facing challenges, offering parenting support, health education, and connections to community resources.
programs.whatTheyOffer:
- Regular home visits by a Public Health Nurse or trained home visitor
- Parenting education and support
- Child health and development support
- Maternal health and well-being support
- Connections to healthcare and social services
- Visits at home or another agreed-upon location
- Services typically last two to three years

programs.name: Section 8 Housing Choice Voucher Program
programs.description: Rental subsidy covering the difference between your share (about 30% of income) and the rent, up to the local payment standard
programs.fullDescription: The Housing Choice Voucher (Section 8) program helps low-income families, seniors, and people with disabilities afford rental housing by subsidizing a portion of rent paid to private landlords.
programs.whatTheyOffer:
- Monthly rental subsidy paid directly to landlord
- Tenant usually pays about 30% of adjusted monthly income toward rent
- Choice to rent in private market (single-family homes, townhouses, apartments)
- Portability to move between housing authorities
- When first moving in, tenant's share generally can't exceed 40% of adjusted monthly income
programs.howToGetIt:
1. Apply through your local public housing agency (housing authority)
2. Must meet HUD income limits for your area (generally extremely low- or very low-income)
3. Must be a U.S. citizen or eligible non-citizen
4. Waitlists are often long (years in some areas); many open only periodically
5. When your name comes up, attend briefing and find housing
6. Housing authority inspects unit and approves rent
7. For problems with your housing agency, call HUD's PIH Customer Service Center at 800-955-2232
programs.keywords: Section 8, housing voucher, HCV, rent assistance, HUD, low-income housing, rental subsidy, waitlist, public housing

programs.whatTheyOffer:

- Waiver of sheriff fees to serve your papers

programs.howToGetIt:
1. Fill out Form FW-001 (Request to Waive Court Fees) and item 1 of Form FW-003; the form is confidential
2. You qualify if you receive public benefits (Medi-Cal, CalFresh, SSI, etc.)

4. Or if you can't pay court fees and still meet your household's basic needs
5. File with the court clerk at the same time as your other papers or later in your case
6. The clerk or judge writes the decision on Form FW-003; tell the court within 5 days if your finances improve

programs.whatTheyOffer:

- Based on receipt of a means-tested benefit, household income, or financial hardship
- Not available for DACA requests

programs.howToGetIt:

4. Submit I-912 together with your application (by mail, or online for certain forms); you cannot send it later
5. Sign the form, or USCIS will reject it
6. If the waiver is denied, USCIS rejects the application and you can refile with the fee

programs.name: I-880/I-80 Express Lanes START Program

programs.name: Bay Area ADA Paratransit
programs.description: Door-to-door transit for people with disabilities who cannot use regular buses/trains
programs.fullDescription: ADA Paratransit is a shared-ride, door-to-door transportation service for people who cannot use regular public transit due to a disability. Bay Area transit agencies provide coordinated paratransit service with regional certification—eligibility with one operator grants access to all Bay Area paratransit programs.
programs.whatTheyOffer:
- Door-to-door or curb-to-curb pickup and drop-off service
- Shared rides via small buses, vans, taxis, or sedans (usually reserved at least one day ahead)
- Service available in the same areas and during the same hours as regular fixed-route transit
- Regional certification accepted by all Bay Area operators
- Personal care attendants ride free
programs.howToGetIt:
1. Contact your local transit agency to request an application (dial 511 for a free transfer)
2. Complete the ADA paratransit eligibility application
3. You may need a phone interview or in-person assessment; decisions are due within 21 days
4. Once certified, you can use paratransit across the Bay Area
5. Call 511 and say "paratransit" then your city name for local info
programs.keywords: paratransit, ADA, accessible transit, disability transportation, door to door, wheelchair accessible, 511

programs.name: AC Transit: East Bay Paratransit

programs.whatTheyOffer:

- Service area covers AC Transit and BART service areas, during their operating hours
- Reservations taken 1-7 days in advance (no same-day trips)
- Fares from $4 to $7 within the East Bay; $6 to $10 to or from San Francisco
- Free rides for personal care attendants
- Wheelchair accessible vehicles
programs.howToGetIt:
1. Call 510-287-5000 or visit actransit.org/paratransit for an application
2. Complete the written application
3. An in-person interview is part of the eligibility process
4. Once certified, call 510-287-5000 (8 am-5 pm daily) by 5 pm the day before to book rides
programs.keywords: paratransit, ADA, East Bay, AC Transit, BART, disability, wheelchair, door to door, Oakland, Berkeley
